name: inprocess-obi-apb-gpio-multibit-f5-pins
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex) and the pinned PULP apb_gpio target; no DMA model is part of this declaration, so the entry refuses F6 by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model)

this declaration is the multi-bit status-vector case: INTEN(24)=0x3 and INTTYPE_LOW(28)=0x5 enable rising-edge interrupts on pins 0 and 1 (2'b01 per pin), and the F5 trigger writes PADOUT(12)=0x3 so both pins rise in the same write.  The ISR reads INTSTATUS(0x24) and the host requires the two declared cause bits (status_cause_bits [0,1]) to be set in that read
the CPU has one external interrupt input, so this is a *status* vector: the two bits live in the device's status word read by the ISR, not in a CPU vector.  No per-source CPU vector is claimed
PADDIR(0)=0x3 must be set before the F5 case (F4 record) so both pins are device-driven; the rise comes from the device's own PADOUT write
trigger_writes are GPIOEN(4)=0xffffffff, INTEN(24)=0x3, INTTYPE_LOW(28)=0x5 and PADOUT(12)=0x3; the entry re-checks each against the profile's register map and the declared interrupt
the source behavior is configs/behaviors/pulp_gpio_multibit_f5_pins.json; the target window is the profile's 4 KiB APB window at 0x40000000
this file declares the scenario; it is not evidence.  The real RTL run under runs/round3-irq/ is the evidence
